title: But what is a Fourier series? Drawing with circles
hook: Opens on a mesmerizing 300-arrow rotating-vector animation drawing a complex shape, inviting the viewer to go full-screen before explaining anything.

scenes.purpose: Arrest attention with visual spectacle before any explanation

on_screen.desc: 300 rotating arrows tip-to-tail tracing an intricate closed path
"Complex Fourier Series" fades in after lingering on the animation

scenes.transition: Nothing removed; title fades in while animation continues
scenes.narration_gist: Each little vector rotates at a constant integer frequency, and together they trace any shape you want — pause and marvel at the complexity before we explain it.

scenes.purpose: Ground the visual spectacle in physical motivation via the heat equation

on_screen.desc: Rod with cosine-wave temperature distribution decaying exponentially over time
Heat equation and linearity property displayed briefly

scenes.transition: Arrow animation fades; heat-equation visualization appears
scenes.narration_gist: Fourier developed his series to solve the heat equation, where cosine-wave solutions decay exponentially and can be superposed by linearity.

scenes.purpose: Establish the core problem: representing a step function as a sum of waves

on_screen.desc: Step function (piecewise constant, discontinuous)
Growing stack of scaled cosine waves approximating it
Partial-sum formula with coefficients 1, -1/3, 1/5, -1/7 … scaled by 4/π

scenes.transition: Heat rod removed; side-by-side comparison appears
scenes.narration_gist: Fourier boldly asked how to express even a discontinuous step function as an infinite sum of cosine waves.

scenes.purpose: Reframe from real sine waves to complex rotating vectors to unify and simplify

on_screen.desc: Complex plane with a 2-D pencil path being drawn by rotating vectors
e^{n·2πit} formula introduced as the building block

scenes.transition: 1-D graph view dissolves; complex plane expands to fill stage
scenes.narration_gist: Instead of sine waves, use complex exponentials e^{n·2πit} — rotating vectors — as building blocks, making real-valued Fourier series a special case.

scenes.purpose: Label each rotating vector with its frequency and show the top-row mini-copies

on_screen.desc: Top row: small copies of each rotating circle labeled by integer frequency
Full-size rotating vectors on complex plane
e^{n·2πit} with frequency integers 0, ±1, ±2, ±3 … and general cn coefficient

scenes.transition: Top-row mini-copies slide in above; vertical separator lines appear
scenes.narration_gist: Each vector is e^{n·2πit}, and we control its initial size and angle with a complex constant c_n.

scenes.purpose: Show concretely how c_n coefficients set initial angle and magnitude

on_screen.desc: Complex plane close-up: single vector rotating, circle shown
c_n label with brace and example value (e.g. 0.5, e^{πi/4})
Vector rotated to 45° to show angle control

scenes.transition: Frequency labels kept; brace and decimal annotation slide in per term
scenes.narration_gist: Multiplying each rotating vector by c_n — a complex constant — sets its starting angle and length.

scenes.purpose: Derive the integral formula for c_0 via center-of-mass / averaging argument

on_screen.desc: Input line [0,1] with evenly spaced sample dots
Output path on complex plane with corresponding sample dots converging to c_0 dot
c_0 = ∫₀¹ f(t) dt  (labeled "Average")

scenes.transition: Full rotating animation pauses; sample dots materialize in both spaces
scenes.narration_gist: The constant term c_0 is the spatial average of all output values, i.e., the integral of f(t) from 0 to 1.

scenes.purpose: Deliver the master formula for all c_n via the multiply-then-average trick

on_screen.desc: Full sum f(t) = Σ c_n e^{n·2πit} displayed prominently
c_n = ∫₀¹ f(t) e^{−n·2πit} dt highlighted in a box

scenes.transition: Sample dots fade; formula band expands to show boxed integral
scenes.narration_gist: Multiplying f(t) by e^{−n·2πit} freezes the nth vector while averaging kills all others, yielding c_n as a single compact integral.

scenes.purpose: Close the loop: show the computer doing exactly this integral to render the animations

on_screen.desc: Eighth-note path being drawn by 101 rotating vectors, then morphing to a gear/nail shape
Top row of frequency-labeled mini-circles updating as shape changes

scenes.transition: Formula band recedes; full rotating-vector animation returns with new SVG shape
scenes.narration_gist: The computer reads an SVG path, numerically computes c_n for each n, sets every vector's initial angle and magnitude, and the drawn path emerges.

lessons: Open with the most visually striking result first and let it breathe before explaining anything — earn curiosity before demanding attention.
Place miniature live copies of the main diagram in a persistent top band so the viewer always sees both the detail and the whole simultaneously.
Stage a conceptual pivot by physically transforming the coordinate system on screen (1-D graph → 2-D complex plane) rather than just describing the shift in words.
Derive each formula beat by beat with a matching animation: show the averaging trick as dots collapsing to a point, not as algebraic manipulation alone.
Use side-by-side zones to juxtapose the problem (step function) with the solution (sine-wave sum) so the gap and the resolution are visible at the same time.
Return to the opening spectacle at the close, now re-labeled with the formula's terms, so the viewer feels they have unlocked what they originally only admired.
tags: fourier series wave circles rotating sum sine heat frequency
